moat_against: GAAP ROIC proxy negative to ~0% through 2021-2025 — no proven returns above cost of capital
Net revenue retention only 102% (Q2 2026) — weak expansion pricing power
Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics and low-cost rivals (Zoho, Pipedrive) contest every segment; SMB switching costs are modest
Per-seat pricing threatened by AI agents — HubSpot itself moved Customer Agent to $0.50-per-resolution outcome pricing
SBC of $514,712,000 TTM (~17% of revenue) is a persistent real cost keeping GAAP returns near zero
moat_for: Unified multi-hub platform — embedded workflows and customer data make ripping it out painful
Free-CRM funnel converting a 306k+ customer base, with upmarket and multi-hub expansion
Large app/integration ecosystem and ease-of-use advantage vs Salesforce in the mid-market
High, stable gross margin (83-85% over the last five fiscal years)
moat_justification: Unified multi-hub CRM platform with real workflow switching costs and a free-tier funnel, but GAAP ROIC was negative to ~0% across 2021-2025 (SBC consumes the 83-85% gross margin), NRR is only 102%, and Salesforce/Microsoft/low-cost rivals plus AI-agent pressure on per-seat pricing cap the moat at moderate.
name: HubSpot, Inc.
one_liner: Quality CRM platform, moat 5/10 — even on TTM OE of $5.48/share the weighted IRR is only 7.7% at $230.94 (IV@15% $85.77); clears 15% only below ~$86, dragged by ~$515M TTM SBC and decelerating growth.
